title: Quasi-coherent modules killed by the ideal of a closed subscheme are pushforwards from it
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $i_*$ and $i^*$ be the pushforward and pullback of modules [def-pc-module-pullback], with unit $\eta_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to i_*i^*\mathcal F$. Quasi-coherent and finite type are as in [pqf-def-coherent]. (1) For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$, $i_*\mathcal G$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module and $\mathcal I\,(i_*\mathcal G)=0$, i.e. $as=0$ for every open $V\subseteq X$, $a\in\mathcal I(V)$ and $s\in(i_*\mathcal G)(V)$. (2) Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module with $\mathcal I\mathcal F=0$ (same meaning). Then $i^*\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module and $\eta_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to i_*i^*\mathcal F$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules; if moreover $\mathcal F$ is of finite type, so is $i^*\mathcal F$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01QY (morphisms-lemma-i-star-equivalence) with its proof (essential image of i_* and the unit G -> i_* i^* G); Modules, Lemma 01BG (modules-lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent) and Lemma 01B6 (modules-lemma-pullback-finite-type), literature/stacks-project/modules.tex, for i^*F quasi-coherent and of finite type

proof.text: (1), quasi-coherence. The closed immersion $i$ is finite, in particular affine [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. For an affine morphism the pushforward of a quasi-coherent module is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change](1). Hence $i_*\mathcal G$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$. (Stacks deduces this from Schemes 01LC, a closed immersion being quasi-compact and separated by Morphisms 01QT, 01QU; the affine case used here is the special case of a closed immersion being affine, Morphisms 01SE.)

(1), annihilation. Let $V\subseteq X$ be open, $a\in\mathcal I(V)$ and $s\in(i_*\mathcal G)(V)=\mathcal G(i^{-1}V)$. The $\mathcal O_X(V)$-module structure of $(i_*\mathcal G)(V)$ is the $\mathcal O_Z(i^{-1}V)$-module structure of $\mathcal G(i^{-1}V)$ restricted along $i^\sharp_V:\mathcal O_X(V)\to\mathcal O_Z(i^{-1}V)$ (definition of the pushforward of modules [def-pc-module-pullback]), so $as=i^\sharp_V(a)\,s=0\cdot s=0$, because $\mathcal I(V)=\ker i^\sharp_V$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Hence $\mathcal I\,(i_*\mathcal G)=0$ (for every $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$).

source.place: Modules, Lemma 08KS (lemma-i-star-equivalence), cited in the proof of Morphisms 01QY for I(i_*F) = 0

proof.text: (2), quasi-coherence and finite type of $i^*\mathcal F$. Since $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent, $i^*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. If $\mathcal F$ is moreover of finite type, then $i^*\mathcal F$ is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type](3) applied to $f=i$.

(2), stalks of $\eta_{\mathcal F}$ outside $i(Z)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks] it suffices to show that the stalk map $(\eta_{\mathcal F})_x:\mathcal F_x\to(i_*i^*\mathcal F)_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is bijective for every $x\in X$. Let $x\notin i(Z)$. Since $i(Z)$ is closed [def-weil-closed-immersion], $V=X\setminus i(Z)$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$ with $i^{-1}V=\emptyset$. Then $(i_*i^*\mathcal F)_x=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks](1); and $\mathcal O_Z(\emptyset)=0$ gives $\mathcal I(W)=\ker(\mathcal O_X(W)\to0)=\mathcal O_X(W)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], so $1\in\mathcal I(W)$ and every $s\in\mathcal F(W)$ satisfies $s=1\cdot s=0$ by $\mathcal I\mathcal F=0$; hence $\mathcal F_x=0$. So $(\eta_{\mathcal F})_x:0\to0$ is bijective.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 08KS (lemma-i-star-equivalence), proof, second paragraph (case x not in i(Z)); Sheaves, Lemma 00AE (lemma-stalks-closed-pushforward), first case, literature/stacks-project/sheaves.tex

proof.text: (2), the local ring map at a point of $Z$. Let $z\in Z$, $x=i(z)$, and let $\varphi=i^\sharp_z:\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, $a_x\mapsto(i^\sharp_V(a))_z$ for $a\in\mathcal O_X(V)$; it is the composite of the stalk map $\mathcal O_{X,x}\to(i_*\mathcal O_Z)_x$ of $i^\sharp$ with the bijection $\beta=c_z:(i_*\mathcal O_Z)_x\to\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks](2) for $\mathcal G=\mathcal O_Z$ ($i$ is a homeomorphism onto the closed subset $i(Z)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]). (a) $\varphi$ is surjective: $i^\sharp:\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z$ is surjective as a map of sheaves [def-weil-closed-immersion], hence surjective on the stalk at $x$ [lem-weil-pbc-locally-surjective-iff-stalks], and $\beta$ is bijective. (b) $K=\ker\varphi$ kills $\mathcal F_x$: if $a\in\mathcal O_X(V)$ and $\varphi(a_x)=0$, then, $\beta$ being injective, the germ of $i^\sharp_V(a)$ at $x$ in $(i_*\mathcal O_Z)_x$ is $0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], so there is an open $x\in W\subseteq V$ with $i^\sharp_W(a|_W)=i^\sharp_V(a)|_{i^{-1}W}=0$, i.e. $a|_W\in\mathcal I(W)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. For $s\in\mathcal F(V')$ with $x\in V'$, put $W'=W\cap V'$: $a_x s_x=(a|_{W'}s|_{W'})_x=0$ since $a|_{W'}\in\mathcal I(W')$ and $\mathcal I\mathcal F=0$. So $K\mathcal F_x=0$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 08KS (lemma-i-star-equivalence), proof, second paragraph: 'O_{Z,x} = O_{X,x}/I_x and G_x is annihilated by I_x'

proof.text: (2), stalks of $\eta_{\mathcal F}$ on $i(Z)$. Keep $z$, $x=i(z)$, $\varphi$, $K$ of the previous step and put $M=\mathcal F_x$. Let $\beta':(i_*i^*\mathcal F)_x\to(i^*\mathcal F)_z$ be the bijection $c_z$ of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks](2) for the $\mathcal O_Z$-module $i^*\mathcal F$, and $\gamma:(i^*\mathcal F)_z\to M\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] (tensor product formed with $\varphi$). For $s\in\mathcal F(V)$, $x\in V$: $(\eta_{\mathcal F})_x(s_x)$ is the germ at $x$ of $\eta_{\mathcal F,V}(s)=i^*s\in(i_*i^*\mathcal F)(V)=(i^*\mathcal F)(i^{-1}V)$ [def-pc-module-pullback], $\beta'$ sends it to $(i^*s)_z$, and $\gamma((i^*s)_z)=s_x\otimes1$. Hence $\gamma\circ\beta'\circ(\eta_{\mathcal F})_x=c$ with $c:M\to M\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. The map $c$ is bijective: $\varphi$ is surjective with kernel $K$ and $KM=0$ (previous step), so $(m,b)\mapsto\tilde b\,m$ ($\tilde b\in\mathcal O_{X,x}$ any lift of $b$) is a well-defined $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-bilinear map $M\times\mathcal O_{Z,z}\to M$, whose induced map $M\otimes\mathcal O_{Z,z}\to M$ is inverse to $c$ (it sends $m\otimes b=\tilde bm\otimes1$ to $\tilde bm$). Since $\beta'$ and $\gamma$ are bijective, $(\eta_{\mathcal F})_x=\beta'^{-1}\gamma^{-1}c$ is bijective.

proof.text: (2), conclusion. $\eta_{\mathcal F}$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-module-pullback] whose stalk maps are bijective at every $x\in X$ (the two previous steps cover $x\notin i(Z)$ and $x\in i(Z)$), hence an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks].

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against Morphisms 01QY, Modules 08KS, 01BG, 01B6 (tags verified in tags/tags); statement and stmt_deps kept. Proof written in 7 steps: (1) quasi-coherence of i_*G via i affine (closed immersion finite, Mathlib leaf) and the affine pushforward node of this unit, instead of Stacks' 01LC (qcqs pushforward; its node pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh lies in sec-abelian-varieties, outside the route); annihilation elementary from the kernel definition of I; (2) i^*F quasi-coherent by a new node (Modules 01BG), finite type by lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type (3); the unit F -> i_*i^*F is shown to be an isomorphism stalkwise following the proof of Modules 08KS (which the footnote of 01QY cites), not by Stacks' affine-local argument, because the latter needs the compatibility of i^*, i_* and the unit with restriction to affine opens, for which no node exists, while the stalkwise argument uses existing nodes (module-iso-on-stalks, locally-surjective-iff-stalks, module-stalk-pullback) and lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks (Sheaves 00AE, created the same day by the worker of lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence; a node of mine with the same content was dropped before commit). The use of lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback (unit sk-thm-reduction; Sheaves 0098, stalk of a module pullback) is a generic tool lemma used as a black box, to be recorded in tool_uses by the lead. New node: lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent (unsplit; sorry-free Lean candidate AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isQuasicoherent_pullback on slopmaster2).
